briefs.c4ee2a1aab6c194d: The question asks whether the first published FRED DGS10 value for 2026-11-06 is above 4.94 percent; a value of exactly 4.94 does not count. Search summaries of a Trading Economics page put the 10-year yield at 4.92% on 2026-11-02, down 2 basis points from the prior session (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield). The same summaries cite Fed H.15 values of 4.94 on 2026-10-30 and 4.98 on 2026-10-29, so the threshold equals the 10-30 value and sits about 2 basis points above the latest level (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/dgs10). The yield is described as near a seven-week low after coming down from a peak above 5.18%, the highest since 2002, reached around the September jobs report. A CNBC piece dated 2026-10-02 covers the jobs-report reaction in Treasuries (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/02/treasury-yields-bonds-nonfarm-payrolls.html), and a 2026-09-04 headline says the 2-year yield hit its highest since January 2025 on a hot jobs report that raised the chance of a Fed hike. No official series was opened, so no count of past windows was made. As a rough assumption from general knowledge, daily changes in the 10-year have a standard deviation of 5-7 basis points, so the four sessions from 11-02 to 11-06 give a spread of about 10-14 basis points. Against that spread a 2 basis point gap is small, so the level question is close to even. The November payrolls report is probably due on 2026-11-06, the resolution day, though that date and any consensus were not confirmed. A strong report or renewed hike talk would push the yield back above 4.94, while continued decline from the recent peak would keep it below. The 11-03 value and the dates of CPI, Fed events and auctions before 11-06 are unknown, and any of them would move the answer.
